mice expressing a mammary tumor-specific p53.R273H mutation (equivalent to human R270H) at physiologic expression levels develop mammary gland tumors at high frequency.

mice expressing a targeted p53(R270) mutation at physiologic expression levels in the mammary gland mimic human breast cancer and provide a well-suitted mouse model to study breast tumorigenensis and responsiveness to chemotherapeutics.
mice expressing a mammary-gland-specific R270H p53 mutation (equivalent to human R273) mimic human breast cancer and are suitable to study chemotherapeutics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel mouse model to study human breast cancer development and the effects of chemotherapeutics on tumor progression.
the molecular mechanisms underlying mammary tumorigenesis, with a special focus on the role of p 53 in breast cancer development.
the identification and analysis of genes involved in mammary gland cancer development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53(R270/+)WAPcre mice provide a useful model system to study mammary gland tumour development and the responsiveness of breast tumours to chemotherapeutic agents.
p53 mutations in human breast tumors are not merely a reflection of the p53 tumor-suppressor function but rather play a direct role in the tumorigenesis process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generated a mouse model for human breast cancer that mimics human breast cancer development in terms of p53 status and gene expression profiles.
the R270W mutation in p53 is sufficient to induce breast cancer, that this mutation acts in a dominant negative manner, and that it is a strong driver of breast cancer.
the p53(R270W) mutation, a frequent tumor-associated mutation in human breast cancer, is able to induce breast tumors in transgenic mice.

the R270 hotspot mutation in p 53 predisposes for mamary gland tumors in mice, mimicking the situation in humans.
